blocks.html:
• Why SSO: no long-lived access keys on your Mac; a login lasts up to 12 hours, then aws sso login again.
#WhereDo
1aws.amazon.com → Create an AWS AccountRoot email, card, support plan Basic (free)
2Console (top right, account name) → Security credentials → Assign MFA deviceAuthenticator app on your phone
3Top right region pickerAsia Pacific (Singapore) ap-southeast-1
4Billing and Cost Management → Budgets → Create budget → Monthly cost budgetAmount 60, your email: a mail when the forecast passes it
5IAM Identity Center → EnableOrganization instance
6Identity Center → Users → Add userYour email; accept the invite mail, set a password and MFA
7Identity Center → Permission sets → Create → Predefined → AdministratorAccessSession duration 12 hours
8Identity Center → AWS accounts → tick your account → Assign users or groupsYour user + AdministratorAccess
9Identity Center → DashboardCopy the AWS access portal URL
  • On the Mac, answer the prompts with the portal URL, region ap-southeast-1, your account, AdministratorAccess, profile name sitelog:
bash
aws configure sso
bash
aws sso login --profile sitelog
bash
aws sts get-caller-identity --profile sitelog
  • Expected: a JSON with your 12-digit Account and an Arn containing AWSReservedSSO_AdministratorAccess.
  • So you do not type --profile every time, add to ~/.zshrc: export AWS_PROFILE=sitelog.

Diagram: Root user, email + MFA, billing only → IAM Identity Center, user: you, permission set: AdministratorAccess → aws configure sso, profile sitelog → CLI, CDK, local API

blocks.html:
• The app's F02 guide uses the same project; if it already exists, only do rows 4–5.
#WhereDo
1console.firebase.google.com → Add projectName sitelog-dev; Analytics off
2Build → Authentication → Get started → Sign-in methodEnable Email/Password (Apple: iOS F02)
3Authentication → Users → Add usertest1@example.com + a password: your test account for curl
4⚙ Project settings → Service accounts → Generate new private keySave as ~/secrets/sitelog-dev-service-account.json — never inside the repo
5⚙ Project settings → GeneralCopy Web API key (if missing: add a Web app </> first)
  • Turn the key into the one-line value the backend reads (copied to the clipboard):
bash
base64 -i ~/secrets/sitelog-dev-service-account.json | pbcopy
  • Why base64: the JSON has line breaks; an environment variable must be one line.
  • The service-account key can mint admin access to your Firebase project: keep it out of chats, screenshots and git.
